questions.question: With no extra options on `fetch`, when is a page's data typically fetched?
options: Once at build time, then served as static HTML
Never — fetch requires an explicit cache option
Only when the user scrolls to that section
questions.explanation: By default, fetch results are cached and the page is statically rendered at build time — the fastest option, but data won't update until the next deploy or revalidation.

questions.question: What does `fetch(url, { next: { revalidate: 60 } })` enable?
options: The page is rendered fresh on every request
Incremental Static Regeneration — the cached page is regenerated in the background at most once every 60 seconds
The request is retried 60 times on failure
The page becomes a Client Component
questions.explanation: `revalidate` enables ISR: content stays statically served but is refreshed periodically, a middle ground between fully static and fully dynamic.

questions.question: What forces a page to render dynamically on every request?
options: Using `cache: 'no-store'`, reading cookies/headers, or depending on a dynamic value at request time
questions.explanation: `no-store` (or accessing per-request data like cookies) opts a route out of caching and static generation, appropriate for personalized content like a dashboard.

questions.question: What is `generateStaticParams` used for?
options: Pre-building a dynamic route's pages at build time for a known set of param values
Only used in the pages router, not the app router
questions.explanation: It tells Next.js which dynamic segment values exist ahead of time (e.g. every course slug), so those routes are pre-rendered instead of rendered on first visit.
